data_gate.checked_at_fit: the worker hashes the bytes it reads at fit start and refuses the fit if they differ

budget.rule: 10% of the worker's RAM (15.7 GB, the host's RAM)

plan.why: a CSV-era version (no __row_id) is read whole: sampling needs a Parquet table (P10 migrates it)

frame.text: trained on all 2,400 training rows; holdout scored on all 600 rows

doctor.headline: Leakage (major): 'debt_to_income' (20%, alone AUC 0.622), 'application_date' (14%), 'credit_score' (14%, alone AUC 0.714) carry the most of the model's importance and nobody has said they are known when the decision is made. Open timing questions: a strong real signal and a column recorded after the outcome look the same here; only the timing settles it (a one-column run without each measures how much the score leans on it). 116 holdout rows (19%) are not new to the model: their customer_id also occurs in training (116 rows). Holdout AUC 0.728 on all rows vs 0.735 ± 0.106 on the new rows only. A split that keeps each entity on one side gives the honest score.

secondary.reason: The minority class 'Yes' is 5.5% of rows and the run predicts at t = 0.500. On the holdout F₁ is 0.158 at t = 0.5 but 0.300 at t = 0.150 (an upper bound: t chosen on these rows).
secondary.title: Imbalanced label

secondary.reason: Holdout recall on 'Yes' is 0.091 against a macro mean of 0.544 (n = 33); 30 of them were predicted 'No'.

eval_metric.name: accuracy
eval_metric.scores_note: score_* are AutoGluon's higher-is-better scores; *_natural are in the metric's own units

oof.note: No bagging in this run (num_bag_folds = 0): no out-of-fold predictions.

notes: added SCORECARD (ensemble_models.scorecard) as the interpretable benchmark: binning (≤ 6 bins, ≥ 5% of rows each, monotone event rate) → weight of evidence → logistic regression → points (PDO 20, 600 at odds 50:1); bins are fitted on each fold's training rows only

delta_auc.method: paired percentile bootstrap over holdout rows
